item.title: What is kinder for her?
item.description: Hi all. Trigger warning regarding being PTS. My mum has a 8 year old JRT, had her since she was a puppy. Has free rein of the house, sleeps on the bed etc. When she was about 8 months she got really sick and she had to go stay at a specialist vets for a week or so. When she came back she was really nervous and we put it down to being ill and thought she would move on. Truthfully over the years she has remained a very nervous dog. Barks all the time, can’t stand being away from her mum, nervous of people, animals…everything really. It’s been really hard for mum but she has managed it, and loves her to bits. As she has got older, her behaviour has just got worse/harder. She is not naughty, in fact she is really well behaved. Was easy to train, wouldn’t touch anything dropped etc but she’s soo unhappy. Since last year this really has got worse and now she has started biting. Due to her anxiety we never touch/approach her, she will come to us sometimes wanting fuss and we give it, then she bites out of nowhere. We have tried behavioural therapists, more than one and nothing works. I will admit mum isn’t strict with her but this just seems so harsh on the dog. She can’t be trusted, even on a walk mum has to be on high alert in case anyone touches her, luckily most people ask and mum can say please don’t she’s nervous. Last week it came to a head after yet another bite, and I took her to the vet. The vet was lovely but said really she has no quality of life and we should really strongly consider having her PTS. There is one more option, she has given us the strongest anxiety medication she can for her size and said give it 2 weeks. If we don’t see an improvement, we should go back and put her out of her misery. She is so sad and unhappy and I totally see the vets point but my mum is broken hearted. We have discussed rehoming options but who would take on a dog that bites, especially out of nowhere? Any advice would be greatly received as I feel like she’s on death row.

item.title: My poor mum's life has been destroyed by Alzheimer's but it's ruined mine too.
item.description:
As well as my poor dad's life and my sisters too. Mum would have hated this.
Over the last 8 years my thoughts have always been for my dear mum, I have gone out of my way to help her on this dreadful journey because she was the best mother but it's taken a massive chunk out of my life and I will never get that back.
I know that I somehow need to shelve this thought process but I now live in complete fear of getting this evil disease. I feel that witnessing what this does to people has left me with a kind of ptsd, sorry if that seems overdramatic but it's genuinely how I feel right now. I don't want my brain's functions to be slowly eradicated, to lose the ability to communicate my most basic needs, to end up double incontinent and have to rely on other people to do the most personal of personal care for me.
Mum has just come back from a two week respite stay in a care home and that experience has terrified me even further. The home was lovely with great reviews, a great QCC rating and decorated homely and cheerily but was the most depressing place I have ever been in simply because it was full of (sorry to say), zombies.....men and women who used to have jobs, friends and social lives. These people once raised children and kept households, travelled and did 'stuff' without giving it much thought but now there is no life left in them, just their shells. They need help walking back to their rooms because for the umpteenth time that day they have forgotten where they live and who they are adn are just wandering. Having to be hand fed, toileted and put to bed like young children. It was heartbreaking and terrifying at the same time. I sat next to a lady yesterday who was at the table just shovelling custard in her mouth as though she was a robot, there was no life in her eyes, I smiled and spoke to her but there was nothing there, she was just staring into space whilst spoon went to bowl and to mouth again and again as though she was pre-programmed to do so. I wanted to weep for that poor lady.
Mum was diagnosed in 2018 and since that time I have nothing positive or encouraging to say about dementia and will now live the rest of my life in fear. Every time I forget a name and struggle to find a word, mislay something or repeat a story a flash of panic will overwhelm me and sink me that little bit further into the fear. I am currently in counselling but it won't help me erase the fear because unlike those who have never had the misfortune to see what dementia does, I have and it terrifies me.
I know that no disease is fun but dementia is just insidious and heartbreaking.

item.title: Some perspective on mil
item.description:
Im 38, been with partner almost 20 years and had our first baby 4 months ago. Never been particularly close to his family. Past year or 2 we visit them once per month. Typically we listen to fil complain about health or mil talk about herself. I find in order to hold a conversation it is either me listening to mundane topics of what she did all day from what she had on her toast to her next food allergy to what she spent on the dog at the vets or me having to ask questions to keep the convo going.They never ask me questions, doubt they know what my job is etc. up until 2 years ago i have lived with my mum. I lived at home for many years saving/studying then bought a house 5years ago and she lived with me and my partner while renovating the annex for her to live in. She wasn’t the easiest woman and i am grateful my partner agreed for her to live with us. She lived with us 3 years then developed dementia very rapidly and is now in a care home unfortunately. had my issues with my mum, psychologist said theres a good chance she has narcissistic traits so hasnt always been easy especially in childhood. Only ever been the 2 of us. Anyways that is some background. From what my husband had told me about mil she also has narcissist traits and anger issues when he was a child but has since found god and gets upset when people swear… some things i have noticed recently and would like perspective on as i could just be being sensitive after having a baby.
no help after the baby was born. They visit to hold the baby. Came to my house and made themselves teas and coffees but not me. Took my seat on sofa where i would breastfeed baby. I ended up perching on arm of sofa despite not long giving birth. Yes i should stand up for myself. Neighbours and friends cooked us food and left on doorstep which was great but nothing from in laws. Supposedly she is a great cook. Others have gave money as gifts so we have the joy of choosing etc
mil bought baby entire wardrobe for first 3 months which was generous but also robbed me of buying firsts etc. maybe i am ungrateful.
when we meet them for coffee she insits on wrapping baby in a perfumed scarf or fleece despite him having own blanket. And not being cold either. I feel it is like an ownership thing of her?? Like a cat marking. She also constantly goes on about him being cold when hes not and that there is something wrong with me for being warm. I wear him in a carrier. She has went as far as to msg me to explain how layers work…found this rude and patronising and could have brushed it off easier in the past. She has kissed him despite us telling her not to. she and sil always comment on my weight as i have lost quite a bit. I explain that it is due to anxiety/breastfeeding. They continue to comment on every meet up.
she never asks about my mum. One day i made a point to mention my mum 5-6times and she even changed the subject each time. There seems to be no empathy for a new mum navigating motherhood without her own. She lost her own mum a couple of years ago. My husband excuses her by saying she just doesn't want to bring up painful topics even tho i bring it up.she hasnt asked about her in about a year and a half. No one has.
she decides on outings. We go to same coffee shop same walk etc. i have complained to husband and he now challenges her but we often still go to the same miserable coffee shop. Sounds small but is very annoying. Whole family just does what she wants. Always have.
probably the most hurtful was when she was was telling me a story about another family and how a dil was asking for the same gifts and help etc as another ladies daughter who was ill and kept saying can u imagine that!? She is just an outsider like u! No one pulled her up on it and husband eventually agreed she was wrong but as usual like with everything else she meant nothing by it. He claims she isnt that bright ans has been a housewife for 40 years so cut her some slack. I find that insulting to housewives.
she didn’t like her daughters husband or his faimily. She hasn’t liked her daughter’s boyfriends since her divorce. She has never had a mil of her own. She has 2 adult kids in the house and disables them. One has mental health issues which i dnt know much about to comment on but the other is fine. She lets him work minimum hours and told him to give up job seekers as they chased him too much to get more hours. He wanted to learn to drive and she discouraged that until i mentioned it could be very helpful since she doesnt drive and husband has ill health. I have my own anxiety issues and psychologists over the years have commented she sounds like she is terrified of being alone and stopping their development so they stay home and dependent. They are both nearly 40. Husband has tried to discuss with her but she sees no problem
she is desperate for baby to go to her house. I am dreading the xmas conversation. I have never been invited at xmas despite my husband saying i always was. Couple of years ago i thought it would be nice if we went to them on boxing day and bring my mum (she would be on her own if we didnt) was suggested to mil and she said its fine if my mum comes but she won’t be doing any cooking if she does??? She has met my mum twice in 20 years. Safe to say i told my husband she could stick it and we didnt go.
husband constantly says how much his mum loves the baby and how she would help at the drop of a hat. But so far she hasn’t. I find it all about her and how she feels. He excuses her for buying so much. Yet commented on me buying some things for baby. He excused his mum as she is the granny and only doing it cause she loves him but kind of dismissed me when i said he is my first baby. ??? Husband keeps saying to take her with a pinch of salt as he would like us to be close.
fyi husband has been great since baby arrived with helping etc. im not bashing him.
any perspective would be helpful. I am aware others have it much worse. I didn’t really care as much in the past as it was a monthly visit but now i see her more often. Husband thinks i am being very critical

item.title: I have autism with misophonia and misokinesia, and I live with my dad who has Alzheimer’s and CONSTANTLY fidgets and makes repetitive noises
item.description:
I have been coping for nearly three years and my nerves are getting more and more shredded 😩 I just need to scream somewhere neutral! He’s 85 and has middle stage Alzheimer’s. I’m his full time carer (DH helps a lot).
He taps his fingers, bounces his legs, whistles, gasps, nods his head, mutters, rattles coins in his pockets, scribbles endless notes, picks at rolls of sellotape, boots his heels up and down on the carpet…you name a random noise/movement, he does it. I have sensory processing issues and I’m struggling. He’s autistic too and has always been vulnerable, semi-feral and contrarian - he really has nobody else. I love him to bits and I am coping, I’m caring for him ok and managing the dementia etc…I just wish I could control my own reactions to the fidgeting 😩. I have never snapped at him - he can’t help it - but sometimes it is so bad it makes me feel nauseous and tearful. I have a lot of headaches since the fidgeting got worse. I don’t know what advice I want really, I don’t want to stop looking after him or anything… I think I just want to howl into a void, and maybe a handhold?

item.title: I am struggling with the relationship with my in-laws and their lack of effort.
item.description:
I am really starting to dislike my in-laws and I’m not sure if I’m being unreasonable or not.
Heres the thing, they actively promote this whole we are such a close family, we are amazing but the reality for me feels so different. They will post photos of the breadcrumbs they throw to us.
Last month I was very unwell, bed ridden for almost 2 weeks, then on top of this I had a grandparent die. I could not support my parent during this time and therefore she couldn’t get to say goodbye to her parent. My H has been running about like a mad thing, he’s been amazing and has tried his best. I’ve had friends help with the kids. But his parents, who live 10 minutes away….nothing. This isn’t a shock as they have never called and taken the kids out for a day trip. But I can’t understand this.
I know people will say why didn’t your H ask for help….this is the thing he must be so deeply conditioned that help doesn’t come so why ask. Really why should you need to ask? I have long since bothered to ask them for anything because all I get in return are solutions of how I can do it on our own.
What is this? Am I missing something? They want family and the good times but won’t put in any work? Am I asking too much? My H has never spoken a bad word against them. I can’t fathom a good word to say about them. My parents were completely different from this, they did everything they could whilst they were able. My in-laws are fit and well.
Going forward I don’t know how to engage with them because this has really hurt me.

item.title: Help me make this Christmas a special one
item.description:
Not in a maudlin way, I just want to make, what will be a very different Christmas a lovely one. I usually enjoy Christmas a lot, but I'm just about to have chemo number 3 for ovarian cancer and at Christmas I'll just have had infusion number 5. So far the effects haven't been too bad, but I'm aware that the fatigue and other side effects are cumulative. Add this to a general lowering of the immune system, so our usual celebration style of either going away for a couple of weeks or throwing ourselves into all of the local events will not be possible this year.
I'm not even sure if I'll be up to doing much at all, even now, I have a few days each cycle where I basically lie on the sofa like a consumptive Victorian lady (I also have most days when I'm absolutely fine). We have no family close, there's just the two of us and that's fine, we enjoy each other's company. We'll decorate the house, my partner's totally up for all the cooking etc if I can't join in, we'll read, watch the odd bit of TV or watch a film or two, sing cheesy songs loudly, may be go for walks if I feel good, but can you lot come up with anything else we can do to make it extra special?

item.title: Separating with a young child
item.description:
Hi everyone. Looking for some advice here.
My partner and I have been together for 10 years and have a DS who is 2. It looks like we're heading towards separating - we had struggles before we had DS but our problems have become unmanageable since. We're both unhappy and have been for a while.
My partner has combined type ADHD and he struggles significantly with executive functioning and emotional disregulation. He often raises his voice at me, loses his temper etc but has never been violent. I would want to coparent as amicably as possible with him but do need distance from this as it's really affected me - walking on eggshells constantly, waiting for the next explosion etc.
I took an extended break from work with DS and have only gone back recently. I'm earning 50% of what I was before DS but I think I can build this up in time.
Does anyone have any tips for a mum starting to think about leaving? We don't have complex assets or anything, so I'm thinking more the practicalities. We were planning on relocating together closer to family and that's still the plan, but how we'd be doing that separately? I'm really unsure if I could even afford a place in my own based on my salary now and with the cost of everything going up, doing it alone feels almost impossible.
Any tips would really be appreciated. Thank you.

item.title: Occupation order hearing next week, panicking
item.description:
Can anyone tell me what my chances are or have any experience of this?
I am divorcing my husband, we have one child. I left the family home with our child to go live with family members due to his angry outbursts.
I asked him within a few weeks to please move out of the home and allow myself and our child to move back in. This is for stability for our child. He refused and said he has no where else to go. This is partially true, we moved to an area to be close to my family when we had our child and his parents and family members do live hours away, I don’t dispute this.
I applied for an occupation order on advice.
He is saying if he is forced to leave the home, that he will have no choice but to move back to parents which means loosing his job, or be homeless.
We both earn similar amounts, neither of us can afford a private rental and paying half the mortgage which I have accepted in my statement.
He is saying in his statement that I can get housing benefit and rent with our child and has done a calculation! Or live with family members but I want our child to be back in the family home. My family members can’t accomodate us long term and it’s crapped as we are in a flat.
He has started financial proceedings for the divorce as we haven’t been able to agree with either the sale of the house or buying each other out.
If I am to move back in I can’t afford the mortgage alone and would need him to still pay his half.
I don’t have any concrete evidence of his angry outbursts other than my statement, no other witnesses. But I can’t move back in and live with him until this is all sorted, his behaviour scares me.
For his part he says we did argue at the end of the relationship, but he denies any angry outbursts or intimidating behaviour.
We are both self representing and there will be a legal advisor at the hearing to ask questions.

item.title: To do this in retaliation of neighbours noise?
item.description:
I've posted about this quite a number of times now, so if you're fed up of me, please don't feel you need to read and comment. Those who have been supportive, thanks so much, your suggestions have been so helpful and have kept me going.
The long and short of it is that since I moved in here summer of 2025, dog next door has barked frequently throughout the day, usually with less than a 10 minute interval, but often every few minutes, certainly all morning into the afternoon and then around early evening and often late night, waking me up. It means I can't concentrate on reading, sleeping in the day, working from home and presenting at meetings is a nightmare. I can guarantee that I can't eat a meal in peace.
Neighbours are 60s female and 70s male. She has cancer and he has heart problems. The first time we saw each other over the fence he apologised for the dog barking. I was hardly at the new house at that point so didn't think much of it. It has now affected me to the point of suicidal feelings. I feel trapped, barking has ramped up to every few minutes and they scream and shout at the dog, her especially to shut up. The weird thing is, when I have people round, they clearly can hear and they keep it silent apart from the odd few barks, so they can keep it quiet.
The male and I have bumped into each other in the street a fair few times and I gently broached the dog barking with him twice, to which he acknowledged it was an issue and said that health problems meant they hadn't sorted it. They both are home all day apart from half hour when he goes for shopping and an hour at night when he goes to the pub. Outside of that they rarely go out, maybe to her hospital appointments every now and then.
As after the second time I spoke to the male, it wasn't sorted, I very reluctantly went to the council who had me log the noise on paper and submit. They also send a letter to them explaining a complaint had been made. At first, I told the council I didn't want to push forward with the complaint as they both have health issues but nothing changed, if anything barking and shouting got worse, and they argued loudly every night at 11pm without fail. The arguing did stop.
The council complaints process is long. They installed a sound recorder but the neighbours knew this was happening and kept the dog a lot quieter that week and it was a tiny bit under the threshold. They're still supporting my complaint and will try again in a month when the recorder is available.
In the early days of my complaint after I'd been in trouble at work for noise background doing a meeting (it was the dog barking non stop), I shouted at them to shut the dog up. That resulted in her shouting back and going mad basically, then coming round, hammering on my door and inviting me round to meet the dog. The dog barked at me the whole time I was there (30 mins) and even went to nip my ankle! She said it was probably past training now, that she loves sitting in the window (where she barks from all day long) and that was it. I was sympathetic to their health conditions but the barking continued and even ramped up.
One night after being woken for the umpteenth time that week, I spoke to the male coming back from the pub at 11pm. He acknowledged there was an issue and on cue, the dog started barking from inside the house. He said earlier that night their other dog had died and thats why the other was barking so much (it was the usual barking) and so late. I offered my sympathies for other dog dying. Early hours of that night, the dog he said had died was alive, had been put outside and was still outside in the morning when I looked out, walking round in circles like it had gone mad, clearly on it's last legs in the pouring rain. No human to be seen, their back door shut. Other dog was going absolutely mad for hours barking no stop. Eventually, I shouted through the wall to shut the dog up. She didnt, but she did come round half an hour later saying other dog had died. I offered my sympathies.
At the same time for a year, everytime the male went past my house he would stare in for the whole length he walked past. I tried waving but he didnt stop. He did after I spoke to him but still does it occasionally. She stares in every time she goes by which isnt often, thankfully.
Since then, its been insane. Dog barks every few minutes, scares my own pets. Talking to them hasn't worked and my mental health is on the floor. I've been off work twice for a month each time feeling suicidal and that isnt like me. I had a perfect attendance record before all this.
I try to be a good neighbour. I keep my TV low, dont have visitors apart from my parents, don't play music without headphones. The only real noise they'll hear is me early morning having a shower or bath.
A few weeks back I was seriously considering ending my life. Had all the plans in place, but as a last ditch effort for some peace, wrote the neigbbours a very polite letter explaining how the barking and screamingand shouting made me feel. When I went to post it, she snatched it from my hand and started shouting at me, saying she had spoken to the council officer (he confirmed she had not) and something about harrassment. She also shouted at me, asking if I knew anything about chihuahuas and to read up about them. I think this was inferring that they bark a lot and are untrainable. I told her the dog was her responsibility and she slammed the door in my face. I'd also gone to speak to the male months back who offered an icy reception also.
She went away for five nights leaving him and dog alone and it was heaven. Dog barked a few times but he kept it so quiet. Since she got back its been insane.
This is where we are now at and my mental health is so low. I dread being home, I dread going home and I am always dreaming of staying in a hotel to get away from the noise. I go out whenever I can but it's cold now.
I have chronic conditions which are flared since all this started. The pain is unbearable.
A few nights ago I'd settled for the evening and the dog was going mad, barking for a good ten minutes, dashing in and out of the window bottom like a demented devil. Bothh neighbours home. I'd had enough by this point and put ibiza classics on you tube very loudly and it stopped. Would I be unreasonable to do this again and leave it on for a few hours while I go out?

item.title: Management role to school hours term time only?
item.description:
Hi all,
Bit of background - I currently work as a manager in the NHS at a local hospital. I work 32 hours a week over 4 days and often don't get home until 6/7pm on an evening. Since going back to work after DS was born, I've got flexitime so I don't start till 10am and I'm able to do school drop off. DH does school pick up so we're not having to rely on childcare during term time, as we've got no family nearby to help. Family can help with childcare during the holidays on the weeks we can't manage. Our marriage hasn't been great for around the last 18 months. We rarely get any proper family time together and we are both stressed as DH has recently been promoted and is struggling to manage his workload having to finish for 3pm to get to school. He is having to turn down overtime most days (paid at time and a half) so he can do school pick up.
I have been stressed out with work for the past 2 years. Things are getting more pressured and I'm getting less time for management tasks. Its a very toxic and negative work environment. I enjoy the actual job but I don't feel like I'm thriving in management. I've given myself 2 years to settle into the role and things seem to be getting harder not easier. I've asked for help and support but nothing changes. I miss being present after school and DH finds this stressful. He would rather be at work longer and I would rather be at home.
I've been offered a new job in a new sector. It's term time only 10-2pm and seems like a great company. Its not a management role and would mean I get to spend more time with DS and DD and be present. It would also get me out of a toxic work environment as its really taking a toll on my mental health. DH could do the overtime and I feel like it would be better for our family dynamic. As long as DH keeps being offered overtime (he has had consistent overtime offers for the past 3 years) then we could manage financially.
The only thing I'm worried about is taking a step backwards and taking a big cut in pay. Youngest DS is nearly 6 and oldest DD is 12 and I'm very aware that term time will only be a benefit for the next couple of years. There is the option for more hours and increased responsibility and a pay uplift with the new role in future. I've been in my current job 8 years and I'm worried about the change. I've worked my way up and I'm not sure it's the right thing to do.
Has anyone taken a pay cut and stepped down and been happier or regretted it?

item.title: Bleeding During Sex on Slynd (Drospirenone Mini-Pill) – Anyone Else Experienced This?
item.description:
Has anyone else experienced bleeding *during sex* whilst taking Slynd (drospirenone 4mg), the oestrogen-free, progestogen-only contraceptive pill (mini-pill)? I’m now on my third month. My GP originally prescribed it due to irregular bleeding. I had internal and external ultrasounds, swabs and a visual examination of my cervix back in May, all of which came back clear. I had almost constant spotting/bleeding during the first two months, which thankfully seems to have settled over the last few weeks.
However, the last three times I’ve had sex over the past two weeks, I’ve noticed a small amount of bright red blood on the condom when my partner withdraws and when I wipe immediately afterwards. It stops straight away, and I don’t have any pain.
I’m wondering whether this could be a side effect of Slynd, especially as my body is still adjusting to the hormones, or whether it’s something new and unrelated to the pill?
Has anyone experienced anything similar? 🤔

item.title: How can teachers best handle bullying?
item.description: It happened a long time ago but I was being bullied at elementary school and my teachers did nothing. At the time I didn't even know what responsibilities the teacher had so I didn't blame anyone else for not helping, thinking it was all my fault for being bullied. I've told the teacher multiple times about it but nothing really changed. Lately, I've been thinking about it and came across many arguments about how when the teacher takes sides it negatively affects the bully who is a kid too. I do understand it feels bigger when it seems like the teacher is against you as a kid, especially troubled kids who don't have enough support and ends up bullying someone to cope with everything. But can't the school or the teacher do anything about it? In my case, the school offered mental support class to the kid who was bullying me, and for a long time I've been thinking it was a good choice since who knows what troubles he had to end up bullying me. But I recently realized they didn't actually do anything to help me. He kept bullying me since mental support doesn't immediately stop people from hurting others. At the time, I couldn't really ask for my parents to help me with this problem since we were living in a foreign country and they didn't speak the language of that country. It felt like nobody was on my side because the teacher did scold the whole class when somebody's toy was stolen and the time I couldn't eat a fish because it looked scary. In the latter case, the teacher didn't know who left the fish in the tray so she probably didn't consider the possibility of me not being able to eat it because I wasn't raised in a culture where we eat fish. But the whole scolding felt like it was directed at me specifically. I now think she was just avoiding a scolding directed at just one student so that they won't feel like the teacher hates them. But at the time, the whole scolding thing just proved to me that she's capable of interfering just didn't think my bullying was worth interfering. There was time someone wrote a bad word on another kid's backpack and the teacher scolded the whole class too. That ended up making me feel like I didn't matter since I've been hearing those words from the bully everyday but I didn't see the teacher do anything about it. She might have done something that I didn't know about but it all made me think she didn't care about me. It also might be worth considering I didn't have any proof of all that bullying. I've been hearing about how adults shouldn't take sides when it comes to kids having trouble with each other but can't somebody do anything about it? It does do a lasting harm. Sometimes when I hear or speak the language of that country, I can't escape the memories of him saying I don't matter or him taking my hands during a planetarium and whispering dirty things to me. I do understand that adult against a kid is unfair, so taking sides can end up with more damage but isn't there something else the teacher can do? All the arguments I came across when it comes to this topic makes me feel like there's no option but for kids like me to suffer.
